title: Rajkummar Rao's Prahaar Gets New October 16 Release After Multiple Delays
excerpt: The Ujjwal Nikam biopic, originally set for August 7, has been pushed to October 16 to avoid box office clashes with Batwara 1947 and Awarapan 2.
body:
• Prahaar: The Untold Story of Ujjwal Nikam will now release on October 16, 2026, after being postponed from its original August 7 date
  • The Maddock Films production stars Rajkummar Rao as the public prosecutor who argued the 26/11 Mumbai attacks trial against Ajmal Kasab
  • Aamir Khan was originally attached to play Nikam before stepping down; the film marks Rao's sixth collaboration with producer Dinesh Vijan

Maddock Films has confirmed that Prahaar: The Untold Story of Ujjwal Nikam will release in theatres on October 16, 2026, ending weeks of speculation about the film's new date. The courtroom drama starring Rajkummar Rao was originally scheduled for August 7 but was pulled from that slot, with reports briefly pointing to a September 4 window before the October date was locked.

Why the Film Was Delayed

Producer Dinesh Vijan's decision to postpone Prahaar stemmed from a crowded Independence Day release window. Spider-Man: Brand New Day arrived on July 30, and both Batwara 1947 and Emraan Hashmi's Awarapan 2 were set for August 14—sandwiching Prahaar's original date.

"After discussions with the stakeholders, they felt that it would not be advisable to release the film during that period," a trade source told Bollywood Hungama. "Prahaar is a special film that requires a healthy window, as it has the potential to draw audiences in large numbers." The absence of any promotional activity two weeks before the August 7 date made the postponement evident to industry watchers.

The delay also followed the postponement of another Maddock production, Shraddha Kapoor's Eetha, a biopic of Tamasha artiste Vithabai Narayangaonkar that was set for August 28.

The Story Behind the Film

Prahaar is a biographical drama centred on Ujjwal Nikam, one of India's most prominent special public prosecutors. Nikam has been involved in several high-profile criminal cases, including the 1993 Bombay bombings, the Gulshan Kumar murder case, and the Pramod Mahajan murder case. The film, however, focuses primarily on his role in the prosecution of Ajmal Kasab during the trial of the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks.

Directed by Avinash Arun with a screenplay by Sumit Roy, the film was announced in July 2025. Principal photography began in October 2025, with Rao wrapping his portions by November.

"Remarkable performance."

— Ujjwal Nikam, reacting to Rajkummar Rao's portrayal in the teaser

Cast and Crew

Rajkummar Rao leads as Ujjwal Nikam in what marks his sixth collaboration with Maddock Films, following hits like Stree, Stree 2, and Bhool Chuk Maaf. Marathi actor Lalit Prabhakar, a National Award winner, plays Ajmal Kasab. "It was challenging—I had to understand the psychology," Prabhakar told The Times of India about preparing for the role.

The supporting cast includes Jaideep Ahlawat, Wamiqa Gabbi (reuniting with Rao after Bhool Chuk Maaf), Sikandar Kher, and Ashish Vidyarthi. Music is by Pritam, with background score by Alokananda Dasgupta and lyrics by Amitabh Bhattacharya.

Aamir Khan was originally attached to play Nikam before stepping down from the project. Rao was subsequently finalized for the role, and his teaser—released alongside Cocktail 2 in June 2026—drew a strong response. His command over Marathi dialect was noted as adding authenticity to the portrayal.

Box Office Expectations

Trade analysts see Prahaar as a strong performer in the courtroom drama space, a genre that has seen intermittent success in Bollywood. Rao's track record with Maddock Films—Stree 2 was among 2024's biggest hits—gives the production commercial credibility, while the real-life subject matter adds prestige positioning.

The October 16 date places Prahaar in a relatively clear window, though the final release calendar for that period is still taking shape.

A Story With Diaspora Resonance

The 26/11 Mumbai attacks remain among the most significant events in modern Indian history and left a deep impact on the global Indian community. The trial and execution of Ajmal Kasab were followed closely by diaspora audiences, and a film centring on the prosecutor who secured the conviction is expected to draw strong interest from NRI moviegoers across North America, the UK, and the Gulf.
